page.title: Settings
page.localOnly: Your notes are kept in this browser only.

importExportSection.title: Import and export
importExportSection.exportText: Download all your notes as a backup, or to move them to another app.
importExportSection.importText: Import from an Anchor backup, Google Keep, or Markdown files from Obsidian and Nextcloud Notes.

searchSection.title: Search
searchSection.findPictures: Find pictures by what they show
searchSection.findPicturesText: Search for “Sonnenuntergang am Meer” or “receipt” and find notes with such pictures, in most languages. Your server downloads a model once (about 380 MB) and looks at each picture; nothing leaves your server.
searchSection.modelFailed: The picture model couldn’t be downloaded. Turn it off and on to try again.
searchSection.ready: {count, plural, one {Your picture is ready to search.} other {All # pictures are ready to search.}}

noteLocks.description: One PIN and one pattern open every note you lock with them, here and on your phone.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.colourSchemeText: Popular palettes, each in a light and a dark version.

customTheme.title: Custom theme
customTheme.text: Paste a theme as JSON: colours for light, dark or both, and a style (fonts, corners, outline, shadow, patterns, note colours). Anything left out keeps the colour scheme’s colour and the default look; THEMES.md on GitHub has ready-made ones. Kept on this device; the same JSON works in the Android app.
customTheme.copyFailed: The current theme is in the box below; copy it from there

editor.title: Editor
editor.noteLayoutText: Clean puts tags under the text and folds the formatting bar away until you open it.
editor.sortChecked: Move checked items to the bottom
editor.sortCheckedText: Checked items move below the unchecked ones.
editor.burnDeletedText: A deleted note burns away where it stood. Off, it just goes. On this device only.
editor.strikeSparksText: After a delete, sparks fly where the cards strike into their new places. On this device only.
editor.insertDateText: In a note, types the date, e.g. {example}. Typing /date does the same.
editor.dateFormatText: How a date typed into a note reads.
editor.insertDateTimeText: In a note, types the time with its offset from UTC, e.g. 2026-10-27T11:23:49+01:00.
editor.singleKeyText: Keys like C for a new note, / to search, or F to pin, as in Google Keep. Off, only shortcuts with Ctrl or another modifier work. On this device only.

quickActions.title: Quick actions
quickActions.description: The buttons beside More when a note is open, and what More offers. On this device only.
quickActions.windowText: {width, select, narrow {What a note shows in a narrow window, such as a phone.} other {What a note shows in a wide window.}}
quickActions.inBarText: Up to {max}, beside More, in this order.
quickActions.barEmpty: Nothing in the bar: everything is in More.
quickActions.inMoreText: Turned off, an action is in neither the bar nor More.
quickActions.pasteFailed: The clipboard has no copied quick actions

apiToken.title: API token
apiToken.description: Lets other apps read your notes.
apiToken.regenerated: API token regenerated. Update it in your apps.
apiToken.warning: Anyone with this token can read your notes. If it leaks, regenerate it.
apiToken.noneText: Generate one when an app asks for it.
apiToken.regenerateText: The current token will stop working right away. Apps that use it will need the new one.
apiToken.revokeText: Apps that use it will lose access to your notes. You can generate a new token at any time.

security.authenticatorText: Ask for a code from an app like Aegis, Google Authenticator or 1Password after your password.
security.passwordSignInNeedsPasskey: Add a passkey before you turn this off.
security.passwordSignInOn: Turn off to sign in only with your passkeys. Phone sign-in by QR code still works.
security.passwordSignInOff: Off. Only your passkeys sign you in.
security.removeText: “{name}” won’t sign you in anymore. Remove it from the device’s passkey list too.
security.wrongSetupCode: That code isn’t right. Use the one the app shows now.
security.saveCodesText: Each one signs you in once if you lose your phone. Keep them somewhere safe, like a password manager. They won’t be shown again.
security.setupText: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, then enter the six-digit code it shows.
security.qrLabel: QR code for your authenticator app
security.cantScan: Can’t scan it? Enter this key: <key></key>
security.saveNewCodesText: Your old recovery codes don’t work anymore. Keep these somewhere safe; they won’t be shown again.
security.disableText: Signing in with your password won’t ask for a code anymore. Enter a code from the app, or a recovery code, to confirm.
security.newCodesText: Your old recovery codes stop working. Enter a code from the app to confirm.

magicLogin.linkCopied: Magic link copied. Open it on your phone to sign in.

magicLogin.text: Once the app is installed, scan it from the app’s first screen, or open the magic link on your phone. No password needed. Each works once, within 10 minutes.
magicLogin.dialogText: On your phone, open Anchor+ and tap Scan QR code on its first screen. It signs in to this server as you.
magicLogin.worksOnce: {minutes, plural, =1 {Works once, for less than a minute more.} other {Works once, for # more minutes.}}

phone.title: Connect your phone
phone.description: Install the Anchor+ Android app, then sign in to it without a password.

phone.downloadText: Scan the code with your phone’s camera to download the APK, then open it to install. Android may ask you to allow installs from your browser first.
phone.candidateVersion: Anchor+ {version}, a preview of the next release. It may still have rough edges.
